[agent-bulk] numucc_em, 35 showers. VERTEX: event_half_span_cm 173.6, so the native sweep frames it too wide; I judged the vertex off the --vtx-span 60 re-capture (shots-vtx/evt71642). Not a vertex failure. VERDICT SHOWER 76071 (205.2 MeV, 13 seg, pdg 11, len 55.1): single apex at the X, contiguous, all 13 members inside 65.1 cm and 12.3 deg. Seen from az+085 it is a narrow band ~5 cm across; seen from az-055 the same object splits into two arms that rejoin - i.e. it is planar, which is what a converted-photon e+e- pair looks like, and it is detached from the vertex. Nothing of consequence is missing: the largest unowned segment anywhere inside 30 deg of its axis is 35022 at 0.7 cm (56.0 cm / 17.7 deg), and 43030, 42029, 39026, 34021 are all 0.3-0.5 cm. The weak half of the call, the part I would let the owner reverse: 76071 also absorbed SIX sub-cm hadron-tagged fragments by pass4_angle at 40-65 cm out - 45032, 86110, 38025, 44031, 87111 (all pdg 13) and 37024 (pdg 2212), 0.1-0.7 cm each. They are in the vertex region and only line up because the axis points back at the vertex. Charge is negligible so I did not call it over-clustered, but they are a real over-inclusion. SECOND FINDING, and the one I think is worth the owner's eye: shower 10116 (151.7 MeV, only 2 segments / 18.5 cm) has its start ON the neutrino vertex - it reads dist 0.0 / angle 0.0 against 10114, 10115, 10117 and 10118, all of cluster 10 - and on shw10116-az-055-el+20 its yellow member set is one STRAIGHT NARROW line running out of the vertex alongside the outgoing tracks, with no apex, no cone and no branching. A 151.7 MeV object attached to the vertex cannot be a converted photon; this is the evt280159 pattern from the pilot (a shower seeded on the vertex/track stem). I did not record it as the verdict because 76071 is the leading shower, and I did not mark segments on it because I cannot name with confidence which of the two are the offending ones. PI0: the reconstruction accepted group 0 = 76071 + 82096, stored mass 125.0 MeV. Both members are detached from the vertex, so the pairing is geometrically sane and I do not dispute it; I store no alternative candidate. Note the usual pr/114 6.1 inconsistency - the display prices the same pair at 79.7 MeV on the axis convention and 97.4 MeV on the vertex convention against the reco's stored 125.0, three different numbers for one pair. Clustering statement, silent on PID except where the note says otherwise for 10116. NOT LOOKED AT: 28 of the 35 showers, everything the scope rule skipped below 20 MeV min_kine_best; of the 7 in scope I looked closely at 76071 and 10116 only, and read 82096, 84105, 41028, 80091, 78077 off the candidate table without opening their frames. This verdict is a claim about 76071, not about the event.

[agent-bulk] other_em, and it is the same clean topology as the pilot's evt284200. Vertex judged from the native r95 framing (event_half_span_cm 73.8, no re-capture needed): on vtx-az-055-el+20 the blue star sits on the apex of a small hadronic V - 61011 (pdg 2212, 9.2 cm) and 61012 (pdg 13, 11.7 cm), BOTH correctly left unowned/grey - and the EM object sits detached about 20 cm above it. Not a vertex failure. shw 6002 (104.1 MeV, 3 seg, pdg 11, len 27.7): the members cover everything visible - a 20.8 cm body from the X plus 6001 (1.4 cm) and, across a real gap, 62017 (5.6 cm) at 32.0 cm / 2.5 deg, dead on the axis. Nothing is missing: every non-member except one is at 87-158 deg (the two vertex hadrons at 149-158 deg, 27003 at 87 deg, 28004/29005/30006 behind), and the sole small-angle non-member 31007 is a 0.4 cm stub 111.7 cm away at 22.3 deg. TWO CAVEATS I want on the record. (1) SHAPE: on both az-055 and az+085 this object is a NARROW LINE - roughly 2-3 cm across over 21 cm, no transverse spread, no branching, no fan. 104 MeV is only about 1.5 radiation lengths so a photon conversion can legitimately still look like a narrow pair here, and it IS detached from the vertex by ~20 cm which is what a conversion gap looks like, so I did not record a PID verdict - but the object does not look like a developed shower and a track reading is not excluded. This verdict is about CLUSTERING and is silent on PID. (2) The weak inclusion I would let the owner reverse: 62017 is pdg 13 and is taken by pass4_angle across a visible gap at 32 cm; it is on-axis at 2.5 deg so I left it in, but it is the one member whose ownership is a judgement call. pi0: showers[].pio_id is -1, the reconstruction accepted NO pi0 group, and there is no second EM object in the event above 20 MeV to pair with - so, as in the pilot's other_em event, the absence of a pi0 here is not a mis-pairing, it is a missing second photon. Not looked at: the 5 showers the scope rule skipped (28004, 27003, 31007, 29005, 30006), all under 20 MeV min_kine_best and 0.3-1.4 cm.

[agent-bulk] numucc_em, 111 segments, 21 showers. VERTEX: event_half_span_cm 206.5, so I judged the vertex off the --vtx-span 60 re-capture (shots-vtx/evt100222) and NOT off the native sweep. At 60 cm the blue star sits on a clean kink where a curving track arrives from one side and a second prong leaves the other way; it is where the charge converges. Not a vertex failure. VERDICT SHOWER 113236 (2498.2 MeV, 69 segments, pdg 11, len 632.1, start ON the main vertex): OVER-CLUSTERED, on three independent grounds. (1) It swallows a straight minimum-ionising stem: 14003 is a SINGLE 110.3 cm segment tagged pdg 13, taken by pass4_proximity at 38.4 cm / 4.3 deg. 110 cm is about 8 radiation lengths - no electron survives that as one straight unbranched segment, and on a numucc event a 110 cm MIP-tagged track is the muon or a charged pion, not shower spray. I marked it OUT, and it is a STRONG mark, not a marginal one. (2) The yellow set spans two directions: on shw113236-az-055-el+65 it forks about 40 cm above the X into a long straight narrow track running one way and a large branching EM fan running the other, and BOTH carry the member halo. (3) The acceptance plot is the corroboration the brief asks for and it is emphatic: the members run out to 153.7 cm at up to 31.7 deg (member_span read back from the saved record; the circles that continue to ~190 cm in the same angular band are NON-members), with about forty of them piled at 100-155 cm and 12-18 deg - the entire cluster-108 fan, pulled in by pass3_cluster_map - while the pass-1 box allows only 5 deg beyond 130 cm. At 150 cm, 18 deg is 46 cm off-axis, four to five Moliere radii, which is not the lateral profile of one EM shower however energetic. What I did NOT resolve, and why the confidence is likely rather than certain: I cannot say whether the cluster-108 fan (85-155 cm) is a separate shower that should be split off or the legitimate far body of a genuinely 2.5 GeV shower, so beyond 14003 I named no further marks. Note also that 113237 (pdg 13, 53.5 cm) sits at dist 0.0 / angle 0.0 on the vertex and is correctly left grey - the reconstruction did keep one vertex track out, it took a different one. Second object worth a line: shw 83070 is a SINGLE 13.2 cm segment tagged pdg 2212 carrying kine_best 135.0 MeV and is listed as a shower; that is a PID question I am not resolving. PI0: the reconstruction accepted group 0 = 113236 + 75062, stored mass 149.3 MeV, from a 2498.2 + 109.5 MeV pair at 18.6 deg (asymmetry 0.92). Since 113236's energy is inflated by exactly the material I am calling over-clustered, that mass is not trustworthy and I dispute the pairing on those grounds without proposing a replacement - 75062 is 160-185 cm out and nearly collinear with 113236, which is what you would expect if the two are pieces of ONE forward EM system rather than two photons from a pi0. Clustering statement, silent on PID except where said. NOT LOOKED AT: the 15 showers the scope rule skipped, all under 20 MeV min_kine_best; of the 6 in scope I opened frames for 113236 only and read 75062, 83070, 67054, 62049, 121231 off the candidate table. This verdict is a claim about 113236. [mark read back from the saved label: marks_detail recomputes 14003 against 113236 as dist 38.41 cm, angle 4.34 deg, length 110.32 cm, pdg 13, tier 1, absorbed_by pass4_proximity - the geometry quoted above is confirmed against the shower the mark sits on, per pr/116 2.4.]

Reading A (over-clustered, which is why I set that radio): the member set spans two directions - on shw8026-az+085-el+20 the yellow set is a narrow line with a HARD KINK about 40 cm out, and on az-055-el+65 the two legs project as a hairpin, so this is a real 3-D bend and not one projection's artefact - and it includes 8019, a 9.4 cm segment sitting at 49.0 cm / 53.4 DEG off the axis, admitted by in_main_cluster (walk_add), i.e. by cluster connectivity rather than by any cone gate; 53 deg is outside pass-1's widest step (25 deg) by a factor of two. Reading B: 8026 is a single charged hadron (there IS a pdg 211 shower, 8023, on the same vertex) that hard-scattered at the kink, in which case grouping the two legs is correct and the real error is PID, not clustering. Nothing is MISSING: every unowned segment inside 30 deg is a stub of 0.2-3.2 cm (43046, 30033, 32035, 42045, 31034), so under-clustering is not in play. pi0: showers[].pio_id is -1 and the reconstruction accepted NO group; the capture's auto-slot pairs 8026 + 8049 for a placeholder m = 128.0 MeV on the axis convention, but BOTH start at dist 0.0 from the main vertex so neither can be a converted photon and I store no candidate. Not looked at: the 15 showers the scope rule skipped, all under 20 MeV min_kine_best; of the 3 in scope I opened frames for 8026 only.

[agent-bulk] numucc_em. THIS EVENT CARRIES NO CLUSTERING JUDGEMENT - the verdict is a PID statement and is silent on whether the grouping is right (correction 6). Vertex judged from the native r95 framing (event_half_span_cm 115.8, below the 150 cm re-capture threshold): the blue star sits at the base of a bundle of three or four near-parallel tracks leaving one way and a ~35 cm track leaving the other; it is a real convergence and I am NOT calling it vertex-bad. shw 14028 (301.9 MeV, pdg 11, 2 segments, len 42.2) is not an EM shower, on four grounds. (1) SHAPE: on both az-055-el+20 and az+085-el+20 it is a perfectly straight, uniformly MIP-narrow line for its whole 42 cm - no apex, no cone, no branching, no widening at either end. (2) It is the far half of ONE continuous straight track: below the shower start X the SAME line continues, in the same direction, as unowned grey charge - 14027, tagged pdg 13, 70.0 cm, reading dist 0.0 / angle 0.0 against 14028. So the reconstruction has cut one straight through-line into a 70 cm grey muon and a 42 cm 'shower'; start/axis wrong is the right phrase for where that X sits. (3) The shower's own body is hadron-tagged: 38038, the 37.8 cm segment that carries nearly all its length, is pdg 2212 in the reconstruction's own particle id, taken in by pass3_cone at 3.4 cm / 19.0 deg; the 14028 seed itself is only 4.4 cm. (4) CHARGE DENSITY: 301.9 MeV over 42.2 cm of narrow track is about 7 MeV/cm, roughly three times minimum ionising - that is a stopping-proton profile, not a 300 MeV electron, which at 42 cm (three radiation lengths) would be visibly showering. Context that supports all of this: the vertex bundle 14026 (pdg 211, 36.4 cm), 14041 (pdg 211, 28.7 cm) and 14022 (pdg 211, 13.0 cm, explicitly walk_excluded) are ALL correctly left grey, so the reconstruction kept the other hadrons out and promoted this one. If it IS somehow an EM shower, then nothing is missing from it - every unowned segment is either behind it (143-175 deg) or a 2.4 cm stub at 46.7 deg (32034) - and the only questionable inclusion is the 38038 proton itself. pi0: showers[].pio_id is -1, no group accepted, only one shower above 20 MeV in the event, no pairing to dispute; the kine_pio_* line (mass 39.8 from E2 = 8.5 MeV) is the BDT feature over all candidate pairs and is not a pairing. Not looked at: the 10 showers the scope rule skipped, all under 20 MeV min_kine_best.

[agent-bulk] nuecc, 38 showers - the busiest event in my shard. Vertex judged from the native r95 framing (event_half_span_cm 107.1, below the 150 cm re-capture threshold): the blue star sits at a junction where the long track bends and a second prong leaves, with 6001 (pdg 2212, 68.0 cm) and 6064 (pdg 13, 10.1 cm) both reading dist 0.0 / angle 0.0 and BOTH correctly left grey. It is the least clean vertex I looked at - on vtx-az-055-el+60 there is charge on both sides of the star along one line - but two prongs nearly back-to-back in projection explain that, so I am NOT calling it vertex-bad. shw 6063 (115.1 MeV, 3 segments, pdg 11, len 32.7, start ON the vertex): the member set is essentially one 31.0 cm body plus two sub-cm bits (34021 at 58.2 cm / 8.1 deg, 40027 at 20.7 cm / 24.1 deg). It does have real transverse spread on az+085 - the charge cloud is visibly wider than the polyline - so unlike evt173819 and evt179611 in this shard I am NOT questioning that it is EM. THE FINDING, and why the radio says under-clustered: on the acceptance plot 6004 (3.0 cm) sits at 8.7 cm / 19.1 deg, i.e. STRICTLY INSIDE the pass-1 box (25 deg out to 80 cm), closer AND at a smaller angle than the accepted member 40027 which sits at 24.1 deg right on the 25 deg line - yet 6004 was not taken. A non-member inside the box while a member sits at the edge of it is the cleanest single acceptance-plot signal I saw in ten events. WHY THE CONFIDENCE IS unclear. (1) MAGNITUDE: 6004 is 3.0 cm and below the 20 MeV scope threshold, against a 115.1 MeV / 32.7 cm shower, so even if I am right the effect is small and calling the event under-clustered arguably overstates it. (2) CORRECTION 11: 6004 is NOT grey - it is the seed of its own sub-20 MeV shower, so this rests on the 'owned by a neighbour' basis the corrections warn is unsafe. RECONCILIATION RUN, and it PASSES: the shower dict reports nseg = 3, the owner-grouped candidate rows for 6063 are exactly three (6063, 34021, 40027), and the shower's own cmp_div reads 'already in shower 6063 : 3 segment(s) plotted -- distance 0.0-58.2 cm, angle 0.0-24.1 deg'. Three ways of counting agree, so 6004 is NOT a hidden second-owner member of 6063 the way the evt280972 segments were - it is genuinely outside the member set, and the finding is not the correction-11 trap. I marked 6004 IN and it is the WEAK mark on this event - it is the one I would let the owner reverse. Nothing GREY is missing: apart from the two vertex hadrons at dist 0 and 6008 (pdg 2212, 3.3 cm) at 79.9 deg, every unowned segment is at 47-81 deg, well outside the cone. Second object: shw 23019 (99.6 MeV in a SINGLE 18.9 cm segment) sits 12.6 cm away at 70.8 deg - a separate prong, not part of 6063's cone, and 99.6 MeV in one 19 cm segment is a track/PID question I am not resolving. pi0: showers[].pio_id is -1 for all three in-scope showers, no group accepted; the capture auto-slots 6063 + 23019 for a placeholder m = 166.2 MeV at theta 101.8 deg, but both are vertex-attached so neither can be a conversion and I store no candidate. NOT LOOKED AT: 35 of the 38 showers - everything the scope rule skipped below 20 MeV min_kine_best - and of the 3 in scope I opened frames for 6063 only, reading 23019 and 51038 (66.7 MeV, pdg 13) off the candidate table. This verdict is a claim about 6063, not about the event. [mark read back from the saved label: marks_detail recomputes 6004 against 6063 as dist 8.74 cm, angle 19.11 deg, length 2.99 cm, tier 1, absorbed_by null, owner 6004 - confirming both the geometry quoted above and that no gate ever took it.]
